categories.summary: The collector still rates the suspected China campaign as strong and touching Australia; governments have blamed China for some of it (for example the ongoing EU Commission hack), but no Australian attack in it is confirmed. Gatwick Airport in the UK reports a payment system data breach. The UK says it headed off attacks on supermarket fridges after freezers were hacked in seven European countries. Some linked items (AI election ads, a Visa product launch, a deepfake video in India) are not attacks. Australian phones, banks and the grid are normal.

drivers: A run of big overseas hacks and outages continues: this week the EU Commission confirmed a data leak from an ongoing attack, after Visa/Mastercard/JPMorgan suppliers, the FBI crime database, Chase, Apple and Microsoft. None has hit Australian banks, phones or power.

Governments have blamed China for some of this hacking, which now uses AI tools to find software flaws fast. If it is one deliberate campaign, the likely aim is quiet footholds in allies' phone, power and water networks ahead of any Taiwan crisis, with phone networks, utilities and ports the likely next targets; this is a hypothesis.
Suspected Iran-linked attacks on shop freezers and small water systems remain in Europe and the US.

headline: Fire danger in the Hills is High today and tomorrow, while Iran's claim that three tankers hit mines in Hormuz on Tuesday is still not confirmed.
summary: No new confirmed attacks on ships or US bases in the Gulf were found overnight; Hormuz stays almost shut and oil eased again to about US$88. Fire danger in the Mount Lofty Ranges is High today and Thursday (about 28-29°C, gusty winds), with no fire ban and no CFS warnings near home. Overseas hacking continues (Gatwick Airport in the UK reports a payment data breach), but Australian phones, banks and power are normal.
